chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, he said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, he said: I heard Malik ibn Anas the jurist say:

By God, my eye has not seen anyone more virtuous than Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) in asceticism, goodness, worship, and piety. I used to visit him and he would honor me and turn his attention to me. So one day I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the reward of one who fasts a day in Rajab out of faith and anticipation of reward?

He said - and by God, whenever he spoke, he spoke the truth -: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever fasts a day in Rajab out of faith and anticipation of reward will be forgiven." So I said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, what is the reward of one who fasts a day in Sha'ban? He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever fasts a day in Sha'ban out of faith and anticipation of reward will be forgiven."

key_terms.إيمانا واحتسابا: In faith and anticipation - sincerity of belief and expectation of divine reward
key_terms.زهد: Zuhd - Asceticism, detachment from worldly pleasures
key_terms.غفر له: Will be forgiven - divine pardon for sins
key_terms.ورع: Wara' - Scrupulous piety, meticulous avoidance of the doubtful

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting in Rajab and Sha'ban according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Saduq, the famous Sunni jurist Malik ibn Anas testifies to the unparalleled asceticism, virtue, worship, and piety of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS). During one of his visits, Malik asks the Imam about the reward of fasting in the months of Rajab and Sha'ban, and in both cases the Imam narrates through his forefathers that the Prophet (SAWW) promised divine forgiveness for whoever fasts a day in either month out of faith and anticipation of reward. This narration is significant both as a testimony to the Imam's character from a major Sunni authority and for its encouragement of voluntary fasting in these sacred months.
